correctness.rationale: After normalizing an eight-point spectral pair, orthogonality makes the seven nonfirst plus-position triples a Steiner triple system on seven points. Their pairwise-intersection structure is the Fano plane, so the eight sign rows are closed under pointwise multiplication. Modulo the annihilator \(K\) of the spectrum, the image of the eight points is therefore an eight-element additive subspace, and the original set is a transversal for \(K\) in its preimage; adjoining a linear complement gives a subspace tiling partner. Smaller possible Hadamard orders below twelve are only 1, 2, 4, and 8, and the four-point case tiles. Fresh independent enumeration found all 30 labeled Fano-plane systems and verified row closure; an independently built Paley order-12 matrix was Hadamard with dephased binary rank 10, giving the known non-tile because 12 does not divide \(2^{10}\).

value.rationale: The theorem replaces dimension-bounded computation by a dimension-free structural classification at the first unresolved power-of-two cardinality and pins the exact minimum size of a binary spectral non-tile. A subspace complement is stronger and more reusable than mere existence of some tiling partner.
residual_risks: The order-eight Hadamard equivalence class is classical, so an older source could contain the same quotient-to-subspace corollary under graph-set terminology even though targeted searches and the principal finite-field papers did not reveal it.

final_claim: Across all finite-dimensional binary vector spaces, every spectral set with fewer than twelve points tiles; in particular every eight-point spectral set has a linear-subspace tiling complement. Cardinality twelve is sharp via the known order-12 Hadamard spectral pair in \(\mathbb F_2^{10}\).
limitations: The theorem does not settle all spectral-versus-tiling questions in binary dimensions seven through nine or classify spectral sets of size sixteen and above.
